text:
marco: quick policy q  can i book a cheaper personal non-refundable flight and get reimbursed up to the corporate fare? travel portal shows $650 but found $420 on a consumer site. saving company money but it's non-refundable + no change option.
aj: short answer: yes with manager pre-approval AND travel-team notice. we prefer portal fares because of duty-of-care and easier changes. if you choose personal fare you must: 1) get pre-approval in the travel request, 2) attach price comparison screenshot, 3) agree company won't cover change fees.
sarah: add VAT/tax note: for international flights booked personally, we can only reimburse the net fare paid. any recoverable VAT/airport taxes may require invoice — usually the ticket is all-inclusive so just submit the card charge.
emily: if you want the company to guarantee changes, book through portal. otherwise the company reimburses actual out-of-pocket up to the lowest available vetted corporate fare at time of booking.
marco: how do i show the portal fare? i can't easily pull it into Expensify.
aj: take a screenshot of portal flight page showing price + timestamp, upload with receipt. use travel request thread id as the reference in the receipt comment.
marco: and hotel upgrades? my manager ok'd an upgrade to premium economy because of long haul. is that covered?
sarah: premium economy requires explicit manager approval in travel request. if approved, company covers incremental cost. if you book on personal card, attach approval and explain in receipt.
emily: small nuance: if upgrade is at check-in and you pay on the spot, keep itemized receipt showing the upgrade line. corporate card can't be used retroactively.
marco: tipping/customs in-country notes? i had a porter fee and local SIM on company card but it was for a personal day.
aj: porter tips for business days are reimbursable (attach receipt or note). SIMs only reimbursed if pre-approved for business connectivity. personal-day charges not reimbursable.
marco: one more  per-diem vs actuals for international day rates: if i claim per-diem, do i still upload meal receipts?
sarah: don't upload meal receipts if taking full per-diem for that day. if mixing (some meals on company card), upload receipts and indicate partial per-diem in the Expensify comment.
marco: what's the approval threshold? manager vs finance?
aj: managers approve trips and reimbursements up to $500. Anything > $500 or out-of-policy flags routes to Finance for final sign-off.
people-ops-bot: automated note: "Reminder: All trips must have a travel request in Confluence Travel Requests before booking to qualify for auto-authorized per-diem and corporate card use."
marco: thanks all. i'll file the travel request, attach portal screenshot and manager approval, and mark the flight as personal-booked-with-approval. :white_check_mark:
